THE INPUT STAYS OUT: this ledger and everything committed become public. The input that showed the defect, and any route to it, appear in no ledger line, commit, test, doc or report. Reviewers name it only as 'the freezing input'. Tests use a neutral stand-in that holds the lock, a plain Python integer power in a helper under tests/, reached by no verifier. Nothing that could freeze the engine is ever sent to the box or to any live service.

RED FIRST: a test shows the defect with the stand-in, bounded by a kill: run on a thread as today, a heartbeat thread stops and the window does not fire. The same test shows cells on: the heartbeat keeps beating, /health answers during the read, the read sheds at the window to the ERROR it sheds to now, never a verdict, and the next claim reads normally. With as many stuck reads as there are cells, each is killed at its window, a further read gets today's busy ERROR at once, and the service recovers with no restart. These run on Linux in CI and on Windows locally.

CELLS: a new module src/concordance/cells.py runs reads in worker processes that can be killed. On timeout the cell is killed and its slot freed, so no slot outlives its cell, which is the flaw in today's comment that a timed-out worker keeps its slot. _call_with_timeout's two call sites, verify_math and verify_domain, go through it; the lambda in verify_domain becomes a named function. Workers are pure: a cell reads and returns plain data and writes nothing, so seals, the ledger, the CAS and every other write stay in the front process and keep their ordering. A cell that dies, returns what cannot be read, or fails to start is ERROR, never a verdict. On Linux a forkserver preloading the heavy libraries, so cells share pages and start in milliseconds; on Windows spawn. The start method is measured, not assumed.

THE WALL: serve() turns cells on, and the front process never imports sympy, numpy or scipy. A test proves it: in a child process it calls route() for every public route with benign input, /verify, /audit, /discern, /scribe, /mcp tools, /find, /schema, /capabilities, /seal and the receipt pages, then asserts none of those modules is in sys.modules. Anything that needs them moves into a cell or is a named miss with a reason. This turns 'we mapped the routes' into a fact that fails when a future change breaks it.

DECOMPOSE: a cell has a life. Stuck, it is killed at the window. Used, it retires after a bounded number of reads, so sympy's caches do not grow without end. Unused, it retires after a bounded idle time, so its memory goes back to a box that has little. New cells start on demand and fill the space. The count of live cells never passes CONCORDANCE_VERIFY_WORKERS. Tests pin each of the three exits and that a retired cell's slot is reused. On Linux each cell has a memory wall, RLIMIT_AS, so a read that allocates past it dies alone and sheds to ERROR; the bound is measured against numpy and scipy's own virtual size, and where it cannot be set it is a named miss.

SAME READINGS: library use does not change. derivation.verify called as a library stays on today's path unless serve() or an explicit call turns cells on, so no importing script spawns processes, and the moat, the suite and the integrations keep their path. The moat read through cells gives the same verdict on every case as in process, 1,796 with 0 FP and 0 FN, in a slow test or a tools/benchmark.py flag. Status, detail, data and refutations keep their shape.

WATCHDOG: a second, independent way to stay alive. deploy/nh-v3.service gains WatchdogSec with NotifyAccess=main, and a thread in the serve process sends WATCHDOG=1 by the plain NOTIFY_SOCKET protocol, no new dependency, only after its own read of /health answers. After the ship the lead proves it once on the box with SIGSTOP on the main process, about one window of downtime, no request involved, and records the restart.

ROLLBACK: deploy/install.sh today restores the checkout on a failed gate or health check but leaves the new unit in place and does not restart. MEMORY: the box has little room. Measure the idle and busy memory of the front, the forkserver and each cell, before and after, on Linux, by PSS where available. The lead reads free memory on the box before the ship, read-only. CONCORDANCE_VERIFY_WORKERS keeps its name; its default is chosen from those numbers and the choice is stated. findings: deploy/install.sh:36-37: a rollback can lose every seal. It moves the only data/ and .env into $PREV, then deletes $DEST before putting the old code back. If that rm -rf fails, or is interrupted with .git still present, the script exits 1 with no human warning and restarts the service with no data/, and the next install runs rm -rf "$PREV" at line 62 and exits 0. A failed mv of .env does the same with exit 3 and a message saying both are left as they are, which is false. Reproduced with the step Box and a failing rm or mv stub: seal-from-before and .env were gone from every path after the second run. Swap the code first and delete last, make every failed step exit 3, and have line 62 refuse when $DEST has no data/.

deploy/install.sh:80: a failed --json gate leaves data/benchmark_last.json at 0 bytes. The redirect truncates it before the run, and a rollback no longer restores data/, so /capabilities reads no benchmark and trust is unavailable until the next install. The rollback on main restored it, so this is a regression on a failed gate. Reproduced with the step Box: 0 bytes after exit 1. test_a_failed_gate_rolls_back_and_restarts[json] never looks at the file. Write to a temporary name and mv on success.
